L24: ## Abstract
L25: 
L26: This CSS module describes a way for authors to animate the values of CSS properties over time, using keyframes. The behavior of these keyframe animations can be controlled by specifying their duration, number of repeats, and repeating behavior.

L84: ## 1. Delta specification
L85: 
L86: This is a delta specification, meaning that it currently contains only the differences from CSS Animations Level 1 【66†[CSS3-ANIMATIONS]】. Once the Level 1 specification is closer to complete, it will be merged with the additions here into a complete level 2 specification.
L87: ## 2. Animations
L88: 
L89: Changes to any of the animation properties defined in this specification cause the corresponding `【67†CSSAnimation】` object and its associated objects to be updated according to the correspondence between these properties and Web Animations concepts defined in 【23†§ 3 Assembling Keyframes】.
L90: 
L91: However, if the author modifies the animation using the Web Animations programming interface, the changes from the programming interface take precedence as follows:
L92:   * After a successful call to `【68†setKeyframes()】` on the `【69†KeyframeEffect】` associated with a `【67†CSSAnimation】`, any subsequent change to matching 【70†@keyframes】 rules or the resolved value of the 【71†animation-timing-function】 property for the target element will not be reflected in that animation.
L93: 
L94: However, if the last matching 【70†@keyframes】 rule is removed the animation must still be canceled.
L95:   * After a successful call to `【72†updateTiming()】` on the `【69†KeyframeEffect】` associated with a `【67†CSSAnimation】`, for each property included in the `【73†timing】` parameter, any subsequent change to a corresponding animation property will not be reflected in that animation.
L96: For example, calling `cssAnimation.effect.updateTiming({ duration: 1000 })` would cause subsequent changes to 【74†animation-duration】 to be ignored whilst changes to 【75†animation-delay】 would still be reflected in the `【69†KeyframeEffect】`’s timing.

L71: ## 1. Introduction
L72: 
L73: This section is not normative.
L74: 
L75: Large documents or applications (and even small ones) can contain quite a bit of CSS. Many of the values in the CSS file will be duplicate data; for example, a site may establish a color scheme and reuse three or four colors throughout the site. Altering this data can be difficult and error-prone, since it’s scattered throughout the CSS file (and possibly across multiple files), and may not be amenable to Find-and-Replace.
L76: This module introduces a family of custom author-defined properties known collectively as 【54†custom properties】, which allow an author to assign arbitrary values to a property with an author-chosen name, and the 【55†var()】 function, which allow an author to then use those values in other properties elsewhere in the document.
L77: This makes it easier to read large files, as seemingly-arbitrary values now have informative names, and makes editing such files much easier and less error-prone, as one only has to change the value once, in the custom property, and the change will propagate to all uses of that variable automatically.
L78: ### 1.1. Value Definitions
L79: 
L80: This specification follows the 【56†CSS property definition conventions†www.w3.org】 from 【57†[CSS2]】 using the 【58†value definition syntax†www.w3.org】 from 【59†[CSS-VALUES-3]】. Value types not defined in this specification are defined in CSS Values & Units 【59†[CSS-VALUES-3]】. Combination with other CSS modules may expand the definitions of these value types.
L81: In addition to the property-specific values listed in their definitions, all properties defined in this specification also accept the 【60†CSS-wide keywords】 as their property value. For readability they have not been repeated explicitly.
L82: ## 2. Defining Custom Properties: the --* family of properties
L83: 
L84: This specification defines an open-ended set of properties called 【54†custom properties】, which, among other things, are used to define the 【61†substitution value】 of 【55†var()】 functions.
L85: Name:  | --*
L86: 【62†Value:†www.w3.org】  | 【63†<declaration-value>】【64†?】
L87: 【65†Initial:†www.w3.org】  | the 【66†guaranteed-invalid value】
L88: 【67†Applies to:†www.w3.org】  | all elements and all pseudo-elements (including those with restricted property lists)
L89: 【68†Inherited:†www.w3.org】  | yes
L90: 【69†Percentages:†www.w3.org】  | n/a

L145:   2. Otherwise, sort `A` and `B` based on their position in the computed value of the 【85†animation-name】 property of the (common) 【90†owning element】.
L146: When determining the composite order in order to sort 【39†animation events】 where either or both of the events is an `【96†animationcancel】` event, treat the CSS Animation(s) for which the `【96†animationcancel】` event was generated as having an 【90†owning element】 corresponding to the owning element in use at the moment when the CSS Animation was cancelled.
L147: Furthermore, use the position of the animation in the 【85†animation-name】 property in effect at the time when the CSS Animation was cancelled sorting such that positions of cancelled animations sort before positions of animations that have not been cancelled.
L148: The composite order of CSS Animations without an 【90†owning element】 is based on their position in the 【97†global animation list】.
L149: 
L150: This differs from the behavior defined for transitions. We should probably sort transitions first, then animation, then use the global animation list. The reason being that when developer tools etc. hang on to orphaned animations and transitions in order to replay them, they should maintain roughly the same composite order.
L151: CSS Animations generated using the markup defined in this specification are not added to the 【97†global animation list】 when they are created. Instead, these animations are appended to the global animation list at the first moment when they transition out of the 【98†idle】 play state after being disassociated from their 【90†owning element】. CSS Animations that have been disassociated from their owning element but are still idle do not have a defined composite order.
L152: Note, this behavior relies on the fact that disassociating an animation from its 【90†owning element】 always causes it to enter (or remain) in the 【98†idle】 play state.
L153: ## 3. Assembling Keyframes
L154: 
L155: ### 3.1. Declaring Keyframes: the 【70†@keyframes】 rule
L156: 
L157: See 【99†CSS Animations 1 § 3 Declaring Keyframes】.
L158: ### 3.2. Processing Keyframes
L159: 
L160: For each animation effect defined by the `N`th item in the 【100†coordinated value list】 of the animation-* properties on target (pseudo-)element `element`, its associated 【101†keyframes】 are generated as follows:
L161: 
L162:   1. Set Defaults:
L163: 
L164:      * Let `default timing function` be the corresponding 【102†computed value】 of 【71†animation-timing-function】 on `element`.
L165: 
L166:      * Let `default composite` be the corresponding 【102†computed value】 of 【103†animation-composition】 on `element`.
L167:      * Let `keyframes` be an empty sequence of 【101†keyframe】 objects, each possessing a `keyframe offset`, `keyframe timing function`, `keyframe composite`, and `keyframe values`.
L168: 
L169:      * Let `animated properties` be an empty set of CSS 【104†property names】.
L170: 
L171:   2. Collect Declared Keyframes:
L172: 
L173:     1. Find the last 【70†@keyframes】 at-rule in document order with 【105†<keyframes-name>】 matching the corresponding 【85†animation-name】 value `name`.
L174: If there is no 【70†@keyframes】 at-rule with 【105†<keyframes-name>】 matching `name` (or if `name` is 【106†none】), abort this procedure. In this case no animation is generated, and any existing animation matching `name` is canceled.
L175:     2. Group together all 【107†<keyframe-block>】 declarations that share the same 【108†specified】 【109†<keyframe-selector>】 (treating from as 0% and to as 100%), last declared 【71†animation-timing-function】 【102†computed value】 (defaulting to `default timing function` if there is no such declaration), and last declared 【103†animation-composition】 computed value (defaulting to `default composite` if there is no such declaration).
L176:     3. For each such group of matching 【107†<keyframe-block>】 declarations, ordered by their earliest <keyframe-block> in the sorted order:
L177: 
L178:       1. 【110†Cascade】 together all of its 【111†declaration blocks†www.w3.org】 such that for each CSS property (except those that are “not animatable”, which must be ignored) the last declaration among all its 【107†<keyframe-block>】 declarations takes precedence. 【112†[CSS-CASCADE-4]】
L179: Note: The 【110†cascade】 will expand 【113†shorthand properties】 into their 【114†sub-properties】 and map together corresponding property pairs in each 【115†logical property group】 according to the `element`’s 【102†computed】 【116†writing mode】.
L180: 
L181:       2. Append to `keyframes` a new empty 【101†keyframe】 with the group’s `keyframe offset`, `keyframe timing function`, and `keyframe composite`. Give its `keyframe values` the set of 【117†declared values】 resulting from this cascade.
L182:       3. Add each 【104†property name】 that was added to its `【118†cssRules】` to `animated properties`.
L183: 
L184:   3. Generate Initial and Final Frames:
L185: 
L186:     1. Find or create the `initial keyframe`, a 【101†keyframe】 with a `keyframe offset` of 0%, `default timing function` as its `keyframe timing function`, and `default composite` as its `keyframe composite`.
L187:     2. For any property in `animated properties` that is not otherwise present in a keyframe with an offset of 0% or one that would be positioned earlier in the 【119†used keyframe order】, add the 【102†computed value】 of that property on `element` to `initial keyframe`’s `keyframe values`.
L188: 
L189:     3. If `initial keyframe`’s `keyframe values` is not empty, prepend `initial keyframe` to `keyframes`.
L190:     4. Repeat for `final keyframe`, using an offset of 100%, considering keyframes positioned later in the 【119†used keyframe order】, and appending to `keyframes`.
L191: 
L192:   4. Sort Frames:
L193: 
L194:      * The specified order of `keyframes` is the order resulting from the steps above, i.e. document order with duplicate keyframes collapsed to the earliest position.
L195:      * The computed order of `keyframes`—​which is the order returned by `【120†getKeyframes()】`—​is found by shifting any keyframes whose offset was specified as a 【121†<percentage>】, from keyword, or to keyword to the front of the list (after the generated `initial keyframe`, if any), and performing a stable sort on these keyframes by their `keyframe offset`s.
L196:      * The used order of `keyframes`—​which is the order used to interpolate and compute the actual animation frames—​is found by attaching the `keyframes` onto the animation effect’s timeline assuming an 【122†iteration count】 of 1 and ordering them from earliest to latest, breaking ties by using the 【123†computed keyframe order】.
L197: Any specific requirements on sorting computed keyframes introduced by this spec should be integrated into 【124†Web Animations § 5.3.3 Calculating computed keyframes】. Any specific requirements on used keyframes introduced by this spec should be integrated into 【125†Web Animations § 5.3.4 The effect value of a keyframe effect】. The above description of the distinction between these sets of keyframes should be moved to an informative note.
L198: Note: Although the 【123†computed keyframe order】 sorts keyframes with 【121†<percentage>】 offsets, it maintains keyframes specified with a 【126†<timeline-range-name>】 in their 【127†specified keyframe order】—​after any <percentage> keyframes (other than a generated `final keyframe`), even if these come later in the 【119†used keyframe order】.
L199: ## 4. Declaring Animations
L200: 
L201: CSS Animations are defined by binding keyframes to an element using the animation-* properties. These list-valued properties, which are all 【114†longhands】 of the 【128†animation】 【113†shorthand】, form a 【129†coordinating list property group】 with 【85†animation-name】 as the 【130†coordinating list base property】 and each item in the 【100†coordinated value list】 defining the properties of a single animation effect.
L202: See 【131†CSS Values 4 § A Coordinating List-Valued Properties】 for how the individual animation-* property values coordinate.
L203: ### 4.1. The 【74†animation-duration】 property
L204: 
L205: Name:  | animation-duration
L206: 【132†Value:†www.w3.org】  | [ auto 【133†|】 【134†<time [0s,∞]>】 ]【135†#】
L207: 【136†Initial:†www.w3.org】  | auto
L208: 【137†Applies to:†www.w3.org】  | 【138†all elements†www.w3.org】
L209: 【139†Inherited:†www.w3.org】  | no
L210: 【140†Percentages:†www.w3.org】  | N/A
L211: 【141†Computed value:†www.w3.org】  | list, each item either a time or the keyword 【142†auto】
L212: 【143†Canonical order:†www.w3.org】  | per grammar
L213: 【144†Animation type:†www.w3.org】  | not animatable
L214: The 【74†animation-duration】 property specifies the 【145†iteration duration】 of the animation’s associated 【146†animation effect】.
L215: 
L216: auto
L217:     For time-driven animations, equivalent to 0s.
L218: 
L219: For 【147†scroll-driven animations】, equivalent to the duration necessary to fill the timeline in consideration of 【148†animation-range】, 【75†animation-delay】, and 【149†animation-iteration-count】. See 【150†Scroll-driven Animations § 4.1 Finite Timeline Calculations】.
L220: 【134†<time [0s,∞]>】
L221:     For time-driven animations, specifies the length of time that an animation takes to complete one cycle. A negative 【134†<time>】 is invalid.
L222: 
L223: For 【147†scroll-driven animations】, treated as 【142†auto】.
L224: If the 【151†used】 【74†animation-duration】 is 0s, the animation itself still occurs (instantaneously). The animation’s start and end events are still fired. If 【152†animation-fill-mode】 is set to backwards or both, the first frame of the animation (as defined by 【153†animation-direction】) will be displayed during the 【75†animation-delay】; and if animation-fill-mode is set to forwards or both, the last frame of the animation (as defined by animation-direction) will be displayed after the animation-delay.
L225: However, if animation-fill-mode is set to 【154†none】 the keyframes of the animation animation will have no noticeable effect.
L226: For backwards-compatibility with Level 1, when the 【102†computed value】 of 【86†animation-timeline】 is 【155†auto】 (i.e. only one list value, and that value being auto), the 【156†resolved value】 of 【142†auto】 for 【74†animation-duration】 is 0s whenever its 【151†used value】 would also be 0s.
L227: ### 4.2. The 【71†animation-timing-function】 property
L228: 
L229: The 【71†animation-timing-function】 is used to determine the 【157†timing function】 applied to each 【101†keyframe】 as defined in 【23†§ 3 Assembling Keyframes】.
L230: 
L231: ### 4.3. The 【149†animation-iteration-count】 property
L232: 
L233: The 【149†animation-iteration-count】 property specifies the 【122†iteration count】 of the animation’s associated 【146†animation effect】.
L234: ### 4.4. The 【153†animation-direction】 property
L235: 
L236: The 【153†animation-direction】 property specifies the 【158†playback direction】 of the animation’s associated 【146†animation effect】.
L237: ### 4.5. The 【78†animation-play-state】 property
L238: 
L239: The 【78†animation-play-state】 is used to pause or play the animation.
L240: 
L241: If at any time, including when the animation is first generated, the resolved value of 【78†animation-play-state】 corresponding to an animation is newly 【159†running】, the implementation must run the procedure to 【160†play an animation】 for the given animation with the `auto-rewind flag` set to false.
L242: If at any time, including when the animation is first generated, the resolved value of 【78†animation-play-state】 corresponding to an animation is newly 【161†paused】, the implementation must run the procedure to 【162†pause an animation】 for the given animation.
L243: 
L244: The above requirements do not apply if the animation’s play state is being overridden by the Web Animations API as described in 【20†§ 2 Animations】.
L245: ### 4.6. The 【163†animation-delay-start】 property
L246: 
L247: The 【163†animation-delay-start】 property specifies the 【164†start delay】 of the animation’s associated 【146†animation effect】, which defines when the animation will start. It allows an animation to begin execution some time after it is applied, or to appear to have begun execution some time before it is applied.
L248: Name:  | animation-delay-start
L249: 【132†Value:†www.w3.org】  | 【134†<time>】【135†#】
L250: 【136†Initial:†www.w3.org】  | 0s
L251: 【137†Applies to:†www.w3.org】  | 【138†all elements†www.w3.org】
L252: 【139†Inherited:†www.w3.org】  | no
L253: 【140†Percentages:†www.w3.org】  | N/A
L254: 【141†Computed value:†www.w3.org】  | list, each item a duration
L255: 【143†Canonical order:†www.w3.org】  | per grammar
L256: 【144†Animation type:†www.w3.org】  | not animatable
L257: 【134†<time>】
L258:     The 【134†<time>】 defines how long of a delay there is between the start of the animation (when the animation is applied to the element via these properties) and when it begins executing. A delay of 0s (the initial value) means that the animation will execute as soon as it is applied.
L259: A negative delay is valid. Similar to a delay of 0s, it means that the animation executes immediately, but is automatically progressed by the absolute value of the delay, as if the animation had started the specified time in the past, and so it appears to start partway through its 【165†active duration】. If an animation’s keyframes have an implied starting value, the values are taken from the time the animation starts, not some time in the past.
L260: ### 4.7. The 【166†animation-delay-end】 property
L261: 
L262: The 【166†animation-delay-end】 property specifies the 【167†end delay】 of the animation’s associated 【146†animation effect】, which defines when the animation will start when it is reversed.
L263: Name:  | animation-delay-end
L264: 【132†Value:†www.w3.org】  | 【134†<time [0s,∞]>】【135†#】
L265: 【136†Initial:†www.w3.org】  | 0s

L71: ## 1. Introduction
L72: 
L73: This section is not normative.
L74: 
L75: Large documents or applications (and even small ones) can contain quite a bit of CSS. Many of the values in the CSS file will be duplicate data; for example, a site may establish a color scheme and reuse three or four colors throughout the site. Altering this data can be difficult and error-prone, since it’s scattered throughout the CSS file (and possibly across multiple files), and may not be amenable to Find-and-Replace.
L76: This module introduces a family of custom author-defined properties known collectively as 【54†custom properties】, which allow an author to assign arbitrary values to a property with an author-chosen name, and the 【55†var()】 function, which allow an author to then use those values in other properties elsewhere in the document.
L77: This makes it easier to read large files, as seemingly-arbitrary values now have informative names, and makes editing such files much easier and less error-prone, as one only has to change the value once, in the custom property, and the change will propagate to all uses of that variable automatically.
L78: ### 1.1. Value Definitions
L79: 
L80: This specification follows the 【56†CSS property definition conventions†www.w3.org】 from 【57†[CSS2]】 using the 【58†value definition syntax†www.w3.org】 from 【59†[CSS-VALUES-3]】. Value types not defined in this specification are defined in CSS Values & Units 【59†[CSS-VALUES-3]】. Combination with other CSS modules may expand the definitions of these value types.
L81: In addition to the property-specific values listed in their definitions, all properties defined in this specification also accept the 【60†CSS-wide keywords】 as their property value. For readability they have not been repeated explicitly.
L82: ## 2. Defining Custom Properties: the --* family of properties
L83: 
L84: This specification defines an open-ended set of properties called 【54†custom properties】, which, among other things, are used to define the 【61†substitution value】 of 【55†var()】 functions.
L85: Name:  | --*
L86: 【62†Value:†www.w3.org】  | 【63†<declaration-value>】【64†?】
L87: 【65†Initial:†www.w3.org】  | the 【66†guaranteed-invalid value】
L88: 【67†Applies to:†www.w3.org】  | all elements and all pseudo-elements (including those with restricted property lists)
L89: 【68†Inherited:†www.w3.org】  | yes
L90: 【69†Percentages:†www.w3.org】  | n/a
L91: 【70†Computed value:†www.w3.org】  | specified value with variables substituted, or the 【66†guaranteed-invalid value】
L92: 【71†Canonical order:†www.w3.org】  | per grammar
L93: 【72†Animation type:†www.w3.org】  | discrete
L94: User agents are expected to support this property on all media, including non-visual ones.
L95: A custom property is any property whose name starts with two dashes (U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS), like --foo. The <custom-property-name> production corresponds to this: it’s defined as any 【73†<dashed-ident>】 (a valid 【74†identifier】 that starts with two dashes), except -- itself, which is reserved for future use by CSS. 【54†Custom properties】 are solely for use by authors and users; CSS will never give them a meaning beyond what is presented here.

L109: Custom properties define variables, referenced with the 【55†var()】 notation, which can be used for many purposes. For example, a page that consistently uses a small set of colors in its design can store the colors in custom properties and use them with variables:
L110: 
L111:     :root {
L112:       --main-color: #06c;
L113:       --accent-color: #006;
L114:     }
L115:     /* The rest of the CSS file */
L116:     #foo h1 {
L117:       color: var(--main-color);
L118:     }
L119: The naming provides a mnemonic for the colors, prevents difficult-to-spot typos in the color codes, and if the theme colors are ever changed, focuses the change on one simple spot (the custom property value) rather than requiring many edits across all stylesheets in the webpage.
L120: Unlike other CSS properties, custom property names are not 【108†ASCII case-insensitive†infra.spec.whatwg.org】. Instead, custom property names are only equal to each other if they are 【109†identical to†infra.spec.whatwg.org】 each other.

L125: While both --foo and --FOO are valid, they are distinct properties —​using var(--foo) will refer to the first one, while using var(--FOO) will refer to the second.
L126: Perhaps more surprisingly, --foó and --foó are distinct properties. The first is spelled with U+00F3 (LATIN SMALL LETTER O WITH ACUTE) while the second is spelled with an ASCII "o" followed by U+0301 (COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT), and the "【109†identical to†infra.spec.whatwg.org】" relation uses direct codepoint-by-codepoint comparison to determine if two strings are equal, to avoid the complexities and pitfalls of unicode normalization and locale-specific collation.
L127: Operating systems, keyboards, or input methods sometimes encode visually-identical text using different codepoint sequences. Authors are advised to choose variable names that avoid potential confusion or to use escapes and other means to ensure that similar appearing sequences are identical. See Section 2.3 in 【113†[CHARMOD-NORM]】 for examples.
L128: Developers maintaining the following CSS might be confused why the test patch is red:
L129: 
L130:     --fijord: red;
L131:     --fĳord: green;
L132:     --ﬁjord: blue;
L133: 
L134:     .test {
L135:       background-color: var(--fijord);
L136:     }
L137: The reason is that the first custom property uses the character sequence LATIN SMALL LETTER F + LATIN SMALL LETTER I + LATIN SMALL LETTER J; the second, identical-looking one uses the character sequence LATIN SMALL LETTER F + LATIN SMALL LIGATURE IJ while the third uses the character sequence LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FI + LATIN SMALL LETTER J.
L138: 
L139: So the CSS contains three distinct custom properties, two of which are unused.
L140: Custom properties are not reset by the 【114†all】 property. We may define a property in the future that resets all variables.
L141: 
L142: The 【60†CSS-wide keywords】 can be used in custom properties, with the same meaning as in any another property.

L157: Note: While this module focuses on the use of 【54†custom properties】 with the 【55†var()】 function to create “variables”, they can also be used as actual custom properties, parsed by and acted on by script.
